A passkey is a key pair that takes the place of a password. Your device keeps the private key and unlocks it with your fingerprint, face or PIN. The site stores only the public key, so a breach leaks nothing that can sign you in.

read-page.title: Passkeys, explained
read-page.content:
# Passkeys, explained

A passkey is a key pair that takes the place of a password. Your device keeps the private key and unlocks it with your fingerprint, face or PIN. The site stores only the public key, so a breach leaks nothing that can sign you in.

## Why they resist phishing

A passkey is bound to the site that created it, so a look-alike domain can't ask for it.

## Syncing

Password managers and platform keychains sync passkeys across your devices. On a device without your passkeys, you can sign in by scanning a QR code with your phone.
